guia.what: Triggers an action. It’s a `<button class="ts button …">`, or an `<a class="ts button …" href>` when it needs to navigate. Comes with variants, sizes, shapes, states (disabled/loading), and icons.
whenUse: Running an action, like submitting, saving, opening an overlay, or confirming.
You need a hierarchy between actions (primary/secondary/ghost/danger).
It’s a link that needs to look like a button. Write `<a class="ts button …" href>`.
whenAvoid: It’s only navigation in the middle of text → `link`.
It’s an on/off that applies immediately → `toggle`.
It’s several actions grouped behind a trigger → `menu`.
dos: One primary action per context; everything else is secondary.
For an icon-only button, add `aria-label` and name the action in it.
On touch screens, use size `lg` (48 px tall). `sm` and `md` fall below the recommended 48 × 48 minimum touch target.
donts: Don’t use five primary buttons. None of them stands out anymore.
Don’t use a button for navigation that reads like text → `link`.

nucleo: It’s a native `<button>`. The browser handles focus, keyboard, and form submission. Core’s JS is optional and only covers the loading state. A button or link with `aria-disabled="true"` can’t be activated (not by click, Enter, or Space, and it doesn’t submit a form) even though it stays focusable, and `setButtonLoading()` sets the whole loading state at once, with the “Loading” text for screen readers in the page language.
